I live with my wife and family here in Mapleton Utah and I run a company that lifts concrete slabs that are sinking into the ground.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row type="in_container" full_screen_row_position="middle" scene_position="center" text_color="dark" text_align="left" top_padding="3%" bottom_padding="3%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/6" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][/vc_column][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="2/3" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

What You Need to Know About Landmark Lifting & How We Got Started

Our story started a year before I got into the concrete lifting business. I came across a video on the internet of guys lifting concrete. It seemed like some cool technology, but I didn’t think much more about it. Not long after that, I noticed that my dad had some concrete at his house that had settled a little bit. His concrete was about 20 years old, but still in great shape. He didn’t want to replace just a few panels and have mismatching concrete. He wasn’t excited about spending a ton of money for removing and replacing the slabs either. I told him about concrete lifting and he thought that was a cool concept, but that was about where the conversation ended. Little did I know at the time, but this is where the gears for Landmark Lifting started turning. A few weeks later I was working not far from my parents’ house and drove by in the middle of the day. I saw some guys lifting a driveway just down the street. I stopped to talk to them for a few minutes and asked them to give my dad an estimate and pointed out which house was his. They were reluctant to go over and look at the job and just said they thought with what I told them it would be a minimum-charge job. Needless to say, they flaked out and we never got anywhere with them. A few days later, just five houses down, I saw a completely different company doing the same work. I asked them the same questions and had the EXACT same experience. I was blown away by the lack of customer service! Finally, after my dad got stood up again on a bid (wasting half his Saturday waiting) and having called a few more places, we could never get a physical body to go to my parents’ house to give him a bid. Eventually, a polyurethane concrete lifting company came down, and gave my dad a bid. My dad gave him the okay, the job was done, and they were gone in less than 2 hours! Throughout this experience, I learned a few things.
  1. I learned that customer service was horrible in this industry (maybe just construction in general).
  2. I knew that I was good with people.
  3. I also learned, or rather it occurred to me, that either these guys were all bad with customer service or so busy that they couldn’t handle all the work.
I figured it could be a little bit of both. Being a Communications major in Public Relations, I thought I could bring a different vibe to the industry. I continued to research the industry for about 6 months, and with each month working out my business plan getting closer to pulling the trigger to getting Landmark Lifting off the ground. Finally, in February of 2015, we bought our equipment, and we were off to the races. After a few months of figuring out how to overcome the learning curve of lifting concrete with a polyurethane machine, we have become extremely effective in helping people fix their concrete in a cost-effective manner. We love working with people and we look forward to working with you. We want to deliver the most professional service with the highest quality available in our field. Our innovative tools and techniques help our customers save money and the results speak for themselves. We look forward to working with you![/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/6" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row type="in_container" full_screen_row_position="middle" scene_position="center" text_color="dark" text_align="left" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom"][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text][ls_content_block id="1071"][/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]

title: Can my Concrete be Lifted?
content:
[vc_row type="in_container" full_screen_row_position="middle" scene_position="center" text_color="dark" text_align="left" top_padding="3%" bottom_padding="2%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="padding-3-percent" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#221e1e" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" font_color="#ffffff" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" width="1/3" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none"][nectar_image_comparison image_url="1209" image_2_url="1208"][vc_column_text]At Landmark Lifting, we see all sorts of concrete problems, each one preceded by the owner's question, “can my concrete be lifted if it’s…?”. The truth is that most concrete shifting or settling problems can be corrected without removing and replacing the affected concrete. Part of the trepidation is caused by the fact that concrete lifting and concrete leveling are uncommon terms for most people. [/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="2/3" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

Can my concrete be lifted back into place?

The first thing that we’ll be looking for when we arrive at your home, office or other property is overlapping concrete. If a slab has sunk and then slid below the edge of the neighboring slab, or star step, it cannot be pulled back into place and lifted. In this case, the concrete will need to be broken up, removed and replaced. Another example that we sometimes see involves tree roots. If a tree root has grown too close to the surface, under a slab of concrete, the slab may heave upwards. In some cases we can lift the neighboring slabs slightly, to eliminate trip hazards, but we can’t warranty the work. Because the tree will continue to grow, the root will continue to be a problem and will cause more trouble for the concrete at some point in the future. There are other, less common situations that may make it unwise to lift concrete, but these are the most common, and even these are a small percentage of the actual jobs we receive calls for. 95% of the jobs we are called out to can be done quickly and fairly easily. If your concrete is uneven, or worse, sinking into the ground, give us a call now and we’ll have you standing firmly on solid ground again in no time![/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row type="in_container" full_screen_row_position="middle" scene_position="center" text_color="dark" text_align="left" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom"][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text][ls_content_block id="1071"][/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]

css=""][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]When you call Landmark Lifting, our team begins with a detailed site inspection. We assess the condition of your concrete, check for shifting or cracking, and identify the cause of settlement—whether it’s poor soil compaction, erosion, or moisture-related issues. We look for key indicators such as:
  • Gaps between slabs
  • Uneven joints or trip hazards
  • Cracks caused by sinking
  • Water pooling in certain areas
If the concrete is structurally sound and has only settled vertically, it’s usually a great candidate for lifting. Horizontal shifting, crumbling edges, or slabs that have broken into many pieces may require replacement instead.[/vc_column_text][vc_gallery css="" type="image_grid" images="2292,2207,574" css=""][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]While most sunken concrete can be lifted, there are exceptions:
  • Slabs that have slid out of place: If the slab has shifted laterally or dropped below its neighboring slab, lifting it back into alignment is not possible. These slabs will need to be removed and replaced.
  • Tree root interference: Roots growing under slabs can cause upward pressure and cracking. Even if we adjust surrounding slabs, the roots will continue to grow and create future issues. In these cases, addressing the root system is necessary before lifting can be considered a long-term solution.
  • Extensive damage or poor slab quality: If the slab is extremely thin, brittle, or already compromised by extensive cracking, lifting may not restore it safely or effectively.
Fortunately, these scenarios are rare. In fact, we’re able to lift and level concrete in roughly 95% of the properties we inspect.[/vc_column_text][nectar_btn size="jumbo" button_style="regular" button_color_2="Accent-Color" Landmark Lifting uses high-strength polyurethane foam to lift and stabilize concrete slabs from underneath, providing long-term support without the mess or downtime of replacement.

Our commercial clients appreciate:

  • Fast Turnaround: Most projects completed within hours—not days
  • Minimal Disruption: Keep operations running during or immediately after repairs
  • Superior Results: Cleaner, stronger, and longer-lasting than traditional mudjacking
  • Industrial Expertise: Skilled technicians who understand warehouse and facility demands
  • Cost-Effective Solution: Restore and strengthen existing concrete instead of replacing it
Whether you operate a warehouse, distribution center, manufacturing facility, or commercial building, Landmark Lifting offers reliable lifting solutions built for heavy use.

Warehouse Floor Lifting & Slab Stabilization

Uneven warehouse slabs cause rocking panels, shifting concrete, and hard impacts that beat up forklifts, damage inventory, and create safety risks for employees. We lift and stabilize:
  • Rocking or moving panels
  • Panels separating or sinking under forklift traffic
  • Slabs with excessive deflection
  • Concrete that has settled due to voids or poor compaction
  • Areas causing vibrations, jolts, or forklift suspension issues

Importance of Correct Concrete Installation

Concrete installation must be done correctly, especially living in Utah where we have a freeze/thaw cycle and lots of soil types that are less than stable. Ideally, when preparing to install concrete, we cut the grade down to about 8”.This allows Landmark Lifting to bring in suitable subgrade material in road base and gravel depending on the circumstance. Having a few inches of gravel below the concrete allows water to separate from the bottom of the concrete to prevent frost heave, which can wreak havoc on any type of concrete.

Preparing the Subgrade

Once the subgrade is prepped, we are ready to form the concrete. Landmark Lifting ensures the concrete is sloped in the right direction for drainage and that everything is up to code. We then place the concrete and screed, or level the concrete out to ensure enough in the right areas and that it is completely flat and ready to start working with. Our next step is to run a bull float over the top to smooth and bring moisture out of the concrete and to the surface.

[/vc_column_text][nectar_image_comparison image_url="1945" image_2_url="1944"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]

Finishing Touches

We then run a corner trowel and steel trowel after that to begin smoothing. The key is to broom finish at just the right time when the concrete isn’t too wet or dry. Depending on the intended use for the concrete, you might do a light broom finish or a heavier broom finish for more grip if that is what is needed.

Post-Installation Care

Once the concrete is finished, our team can come back the next day and strip forms that could not be stripped that same day. If we didn’t install control joints (break lines) in the concrete while we were finishing, we could also come the next day and make soft cuts or control joints we cut in with a concrete saw. Both have their advantages and disadvantages depending on the scenario.

Curing and Maintenance

Try to wait at least a week until you drive a small vehicle on it and usually about 21 days for a full-strength cure time. Concrete technically shouldn't ever have ice melt placed on it, but during the first year after installation, it is critical to avoid salt to prevent the top layer of the concrete from coming apart. After the first year, you can use driveway-safe, light-duty ice melt, but be careful and watch how the concrete reacts.

First, the existing concrete is broken up using specialized tools that get the work done quickly. Next, the ground is prepared and leveled for new concrete installation. If the old concrete failed prematurely, this could be a result of improper preparation. That's why it's so important to work with a capable contractor throughout this process!

When is replacement better than lifting?

At Landmark Lifting, we usually recommend lifting concrete when the pad itself has shifted or become sunken, but the concrete is in overall healthy condition. Lifting your concrete adds years to its service life, improves safety on your property and also adds to your home's curb appeal. Concrete that is badly damaged should be replaced. Whether it's spalled, cracked, or crumbled, damaged concrete will likely continue to deteriorate as years go by. Lifting concrete that is damaged may not be the best option.

Not sure if your concrete needs replacement or lifting? Call the pros.

If you're not sure which service is best for your property, consult with the professionals. Here's how it works, we lift your concrete and save you $$$

Concrete lifting in Cedar Hills, Utah is the foundation of our services. Our specially formulated 2-part polyurethane expansion foam is also eco-friendly. does Concrete Sink?"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Concrete sinks when voids open underground. These holes are usually caused by soil of different densities being used during construction combining during construction. When the dirt is under the pressure of a concrete slab, the ground starts settling, especially if there’s been erosion. Both rain and snow can seep beneath the concrete to wash away the looser dirt, and in Alpine's freeze-thaw cycles, this process can accelerate shifting and settling. However this isn’t usually the only cause. The most common reason for the ground to settle and concrete to sink are broken underground water pipes. The water washes away loose dirt right out from under the concrete.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="padding-5-percent" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" flex_gap_desktop="10px" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color="#f7f7f7" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="3/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

How to Repair Sunken Concrete

There are 2 types of repairs for sunken concrete:

  1. Breaking up, removing and re-pouring the concrete slab

  2. Raising the concrete slab back into its original position

The first option is expensive, difficult and time-consuming because the concrete has to be entirely broken up, removed. Then, the hole needs to be filled and tamped down before it can be framed in for the new concrete to be poured. The concrete will need to cure for weeks if the weather is warm enough. It can quickly become a bigger hassle to get around than the sunken concrete was.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_column_text]

The second option is what we recommend and it only takes a few hours!

[vc_row type="full_width_background" full_screen_row_position="middle" bg_color="#221e1e" scene_position="center" video_bg="use_video" enable_video_color_overlay="true" video_overlay_color="#221e1e" video_external="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y63yGoaN9EY" text_color="light" text_align="left" top_padding="4%" bottom_padding="4%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="middle" column_margin="default" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

If you’ve stubbed your toe for the last time on your uneven concrete, Landmark Lifting is here to help.

We’re ready to handle all of your concrete lifting in Alta, Utah, and regardless of the time of year, we’ll make your concrete driveways, patios, and walkways safer to use.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner background_image="1014" enable_bg_scale="true" column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][divider line_type="No Line" custom_height="300"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row type="full_width_background" full_screen_row_position="middle" scene_position="center" text_color="custom" text_align="left" top_padding="4%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="middle" column_margin="default" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="2/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][nectar_animated_title heading_tag="h2" style="color-strip-reveal" color="Accent-Color" text="Why is my concrete sinking?"][vc_column_text]Uneven concrete is caused by voids opening up below concrete slabs. These holes are usually caused by different types and densities of dirt being mixed during the construction process, then being placed under the pressure of concrete slabs, the ground starts to settle. These mixtures of dirt are also susceptible to erosion. Both rain and snow can seep below the concrete to wash away the lightly packed dirt, but this isn’t the most common reason. Usually, if the concrete is sinking, there is an underground water pipe that has broken and the water has washed away the looser dirt from below.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="padding-5-percent" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#f7f7f7" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" width="3/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

What can I do to fix it?

There are 2 basic repair options for uneven concrete:

  1. Removing and re-pouring concrete slabs

  2. Lifting and leveling concrete back to its original position

The first option is time-consuming, expensive, and almost impossible at some times of the year. The concrete has to be entirely broken up and carted away, then the hole needs to be filled and tamped down before it can be framed in and the new concrete can be poured. The concrete needs to cure for weeks, in mild to hot weather, undisturbed in order to cure. That’s a lot of trouble to go through for level concrete.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_column_text]

The second option is what we recommend and it only takes a few hours!

title: Concrete Lifting in Copperton Utah
content:
[vc_row type="full_width_background" full_screen_row_position="middle" bg_color="#221e1e" scene_position="center" video_bg="use_video" enable_video_color_overlay="true" video_overlay_color="#221e1e" video_external="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y63yGoaN9EY" text_color="light" text_align="left" top_padding="4%" bottom_padding="4%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="middle" column_margin="default" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

Copperton, Utah

Founded in 1955, your beautiful hometown of Copperton, Utah was built to support the Bingham Canyon Mine. Now, with wide-open spaces and comparatively warmer weather than the rest of the Salt Lake Basin, Copperton is a beautiful place to live, a short drive from Salt Lake City. This great suburb is a beautiful place to raise a family, but despite its warmer climate, you still receive a large amount of snow and rainfall here each year. Because of this precipitation, it is not uncommon to see concrete slabs sinking into the ground. If one of your concrete slabs has started shifting or settling into the ground, the coming snowfall could put you and your loved ones at risk. Uneven concrete looks bad but it is also a trip hazard especially when it gets buried under leaves or snow. Landmark Lifting is here to take care of all of the concrete lifting in Copperton Utah, to make your property safer and more attractive.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner background_image="1262" enable_bg_scale="true" column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][divider line_type="No Line" custom_height="300"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row type="full_width_background" full_screen_row_position="middle" scene_position="center" text_color="custom" text_align="left" top_padding="4%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="middle" column_margin="default" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="2/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][nectar_animated_title heading_tag="h2" style="color-strip-reveal" color="Accent-Color" text="Why Do Concrete Slabs Sink?"][vc_column_text]When a void opens up under concrete, the slabs start settling into it. Underground voids are common when native soil is disturbed to dig the foundations or basements of a new construction project, the holes are then backfilled with looser dirt and then tamped down, but it can’t match the compression of the soil around it. Mixing dirt of different densities, then placing it under the constant pressure of a slab of concrete, can cause the ground to settle. If there’s been erosion on top of that, from rain and or snowmelt, can seep into the ground and wash away the looser dirt. The most common reason for erosion, however, isn’t the weather, it’s usually caused by broken underground water pipes. The pressurized flow of water has nowhere to go, so it saturates the ground and when it finally finds an escape route it washes away the loose dirt right out from under your concrete, creating an empty space, or a void.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="padding-5-percent" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#f7f7f7" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" width="3/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

How to Repair Sunken Concrete?

There are basically two options for fixing your sunken concrete:

  1. Break the slab into small pieces, cart them away, and then pour a new concrete slab.

  2. Hire us to drill a few dime-sized holes and raise your concrete slab back into its original place in a matter of minutes!

If you’ve stubbed your toe for the last time on your uneven concrete, Landmark Lifting is here to help.

These holes are usually caused by different types and densities of dirt being mixed during the construction process, then being placed under the pressure of concrete slabs, the ground starts to settle. These mixtures of dirt are also susceptible to erosion. Both rain and snow can seep below the concrete to wash away the lightly packed dirt, but this isn’t the most common reason. Usually, if the concrete is sinking, there is an underground water pipe that has broken and the water has washed away the looser dirt from below.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="padding-5-percent" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#f7f7f7" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" width="3/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

What can I do to fix it?

There are 2 basic repair options for uneven concrete:

  1. Removing and re-pouring concrete slabs

  2. Lifting and leveling concrete back to its original position

The first option is time-consuming, expensive, and almost impossible at some times of the year. The concrete has to be entirely broken up and carted away, then the hole needs to be filled and tamped down before it can be framed in and the new concrete can be poured. The concrete needs to cure for weeks, in mild to hot weather, undisturbed in order to cure. That’s a lot of trouble to go through for level concrete.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_column_text]

These holes are usually caused by different types and densities of dirt being mixed during the construction process, then being placed under the pressure of concrete slabs, the ground starts to settle. These mixtures of dirt are also susceptible to erosion. Both rain and snow can seep below the concrete to wash away the lightly packed dirt, but this isn’t the most common reason. Usually, if the concrete is sinking, there is an underground water pipe that has broken and the water has washed away the looser dirt from below. In these cases, void filling and concrete lifting in Lehi, Utah becomes necessary to restore stability and prevent further sinking.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="padding-5-percent" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color="#f7f7f7" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="3/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

What can I do to fix it?

There are 2 basic repair options for uneven concrete:

  1. Removing and re-pouring concrete slabs

  2. Lifting and leveling concrete back to its original position

The first option is time-consuming, expensive, and almost impossible at some times of the year. The concrete has to be entirely broken up and carted away, then the hole needs to be filled and tamped down before it can be framed in and the new concrete can be poured. The concrete needs to cure for weeks, in mild to hot weather, undisturbed in order to cure. That’s a lot of trouble to go through for level concrete.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_column_text]

The second option is what we recommend and it only takes a few hours!

title: Concrete Lifting in Lindon, Utah
content:
[vc_row type="full_width_background" full_screen_row_position="middle" bg_color="#221e1e" scene_position="center" video_bg="use_video" enable_video_color_overlay="true" video_overlay_color="#221e1e" video_external="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y63yGoaN9EY" text_color="light" text_align="left" top_padding="4%" bottom_padding="4%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="middle" column_margin="default" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

Do you love your “little bit of country” in Lindon, Utah?

In the shadow of Mount Timpanogos, you’ve got a beautiful hometown, with wide-open spaces and a short drive from Provo. This great suburb is a beautiful place to raise a family, but with the amount of snow and rainfall here each year, it’s not uncommon to see slabs of concrete sinking into the ground. If you see that one of your concrete slabs has started shifting or settling into the ground, there is a risk to your safety, not just your property value. Uneven concrete looks bad but it is also a trip hazard and if it gets buried under leaves or snow it becomes an even more dangerous hazard to your family, friends, and passers-by. Landmark Lifting is here to take care of all of the concrete lifting in Lindon Utah, to make your property safer and more attractive.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner background_image="1014" enable_bg_scale="true" column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][divider line_type="No Line" custom_height="300"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row type="full_width_background" full_screen_row_position="middle" scene_position="center" text_color="custom" text_align="left" top_padding="4%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="middle" column_margin="default" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="2/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][nectar_animated_title heading_tag="h2" style="color-strip-reveal" color="Accent-Color" text="Why Do Concrete Slabs Sink?"][vc_column_text]When voids open up underground, concrete starts settling into them. When native soil is disturbed to dig the foundations or basements of a new construction project, the holes are then backfilled with looser dirt and then tamped down, but it can’t match the compression of the soil around it. Mixing dirt of different densities, then placing it under the constant pressure of a slab of concrete, can cause the ground to settle. If there’s been erosion on top of that, from rain and or snowmelt, can seep into the ground and wash away the looser dirt. The most common reason for erosion, however, isn’t the weather, it’s usually caused by broken underground water pipes. The pressurized flow of water has nowhere to go, so it saturates the ground and when it finally finds an escape route it washes away the loose dirt right out from under your concrete, creating an empty space, or a void.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="padding-5-percent" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#f7f7f7" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" width="3/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

How to Repair Sunken Concrete?

There are basically two options for fixing your sunken concrete:

  1. Break the slab into small pieces, cart them away, and then pour a new concrete slab.

  2. Hire us to drill a few dime-sized holes and raise your concrete slab back into its original place in a matter of minutes!

The first option is a headache! It’s not only expensive, but it also takes a lot of time to:
  • Break up the concrete
  • Remove the concrete
  • Fill the void with dirt
  • Compact the dirt
  • Frame the hole
  • Pour new concrete
  • Wait weeks for it to cure (in warm weather)
It is such an expensive hassle to fix, that many people decide it isn’t worth repairing their sunken concrete! Option 2 is another story entirely, we can literally come to your home and be done in just 1 day. We drill a few dime-sized holes and inject our eco-friendly 2-part expansion foam, which will be cured and ready to hold weight within 15 minutes![/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_column_text]

The second option is what we recommend and it only takes a few hours!

color="Accent-Color" text="Why is my concrete sinking?"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Uneven concrete is caused by voids opening up below concrete slabs. These holes are usually caused by different types and densities of dirt being mixed during the construction process, then being placed under the pressure of concrete slabs, the ground starts to settle. These mixtures of dirt are also susceptible to erosion. Both rain and snow can seep below the concrete to wash away the lightly packed dirt, but this isn’t the most common reason. Usually, if the concrete is sinking, there is an underground water pipe that has broken and the water has washed away the looser dirt from below. In these cases, void filling and concrete lifting in Logan, Utah becomes necessary to restore stability and prevent further sinking.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="padding-5-percent" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color="#f7f7f7" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="3/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]

What can I do to fix it?

There are 2 basic repair options for uneven concrete in Logan, Utah:

  1. Removing and re-pouring concrete slabs

  2. Lifting and leveling concrete back to its original position

The first option is time-consuming, expensive and almost impossible at some times of the year. The concrete has to be entirely broken up and carted away, then the hole needs to be filled and tamped down before it can be framed in and the new concrete can be poured. The concrete needs to cure for weeks, in mild to hot weather, undisturbed in order to cure. That’s a lot of trouble to go through for level concrete.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_column_text]

These mixtures of dirt are also susceptible to erosion. Both rain and snow can seep below the concrete to wash away the lightly packed dirt, but this isn’t the most common reason. What can I do to fix it?

There are 2 basic repair options for uneven concrete:

  1. Removing and re-pouring concrete slabs

  2. Lifting and leveling concrete back to its original position

The first option is time-consuming, expensive, and almost impossible at some times of the year. The concrete has to be entirely broken up and carted away, then the hole needs to be filled and tamped down before it can be framed in and the new concrete can be poured. The concrete needs to cure for weeks, in mild to hot weather, undisturbed in order to cure. That’s a lot of trouble to go through for level concrete.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_column_text]

color="Accent-Color" text="Why is my concrete sinking?"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Uneven concrete is caused by voids opening up below concrete slabs. These holes are usually caused by different types and densities of dirt being mixed during the construction process, then being placed under the pressure of concrete slabs, the ground starts to settle. These mixtures of dirt are also susceptible to erosion. Both rain and snow can seep below the concrete to wash away the lightly packed dirt, but this isn’t the most common reason. Usually, if the concrete is sinking, there is an underground water pipe that has broken and the water has washed away the looser dirt from below. In these cases, void filling and concrete lifting in Orem, Utah  becomes necessary to restore stability and prevent further sinking.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="padding-5-percent" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color="#f7f7f7" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="3/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]

What can I do to fix it?

There are 2 basic repair options for uneven concrete in Orem, Utah:

  1. Removing and re-pouring concrete slabs

  2. Lifting and leveling concrete back to its original position

The first option is time-consuming, expensive, and almost impossible at some times of the year. The concrete has to be entirely broken up and carted away, then the hole needs to be filled and tamped down before it can be framed in and the new concrete can be poured. The concrete needs to cure for weeks, in mild to hot weather, undisturbed in order to cure. That’s a lot of trouble to go through for level concrete.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_column_text]

[vc_row type="full_width_background" full_screen_row_position="middle" bg_color="#221e1e" scene_position="center" video_bg="use_video" enable_video_color_overlay="true" video_overlay_color="#221e1e" video_external="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y63yGoaN9EY" text_color="light" text_align="left" top_padding="4%" bottom_padding="4%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="middle" column_margin="default" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

If you’ve stubbed your toe for the last time on your uneven concrete, Landmark Lifting is here to help.

We’re ready to handle all of your concrete lifting in Palmyra, Utah, and regardless of the time of year, we’ll make your concrete driveways, patios, and walkways safer to use.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner background_image="1014" enable_bg_scale="true" column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][divider line_type="No Line" custom_height="300"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row type="full_width_background" full_screen_row_position="middle" scene_position="center" text_color="custom" text_align="left" top_padding="4%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="middle" column_margin="default" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="2/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][nectar_animated_title heading_tag="h2" style="color-strip-reveal" color="Accent-Color" text="Why is my concrete sinking?"][vc_column_text]Uneven concrete is caused by voids opening up below concrete slabs. These holes are usually caused by different types and densities of dirt being mixed during the construction process, then being placed under the pressure of concrete slabs, the ground starts to settle. These mixtures of dirt are also susceptible to erosion. Both rain and snow can seep below the concrete to wash away the lightly packed dirt, but this isn’t the most common reason. Usually, if the concrete is sinking, there is an underground water pipe that has broken and the water has washed away the looser dirt from below.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="padding-5-percent" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#f7f7f7" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" width="3/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

What can I do to fix it?

There are 2 basic repair options for uneven concrete:

  1. Removing and re-pouring concrete slabs

  2. Lifting and leveling concrete back to its original position

The first option is time-consuming, expensive, and almost impossible at some times of the year. The concrete has to be entirely broken up and carted away, then the hole needs to be filled and tamped down before it can be framed in and the new concrete can be poured. The concrete needs to cure for weeks, in mild to hot weather, undisturbed in order to cure. That’s a lot of trouble to go through for level concrete.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_column_text]

The second option is what we recommend and it only takes a few hours!

DRILL

[vc_row type="full_width_background" full_screen_row_position="middle" bg_color="#221e1e" scene_position="center" video_bg="use_video" enable_video_color_overlay="true" video_overlay_color="#221e1e" video_external="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y63yGoaN9EY" text_color="light" text_align="left" top_padding="4%" bottom_padding="4%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="middle" column_margin="default" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

If you’ve stubbed your toe for the last time on your uneven concrete, Landmark Lifting is here to help.

We’re ready to handle all of your concrete lifting in Payson, Utah, and regardless of the time of year, we’ll make your concrete driveways, patios, and walkways safer to use.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner background_image="1014" enable_bg_scale="true" column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][divider line_type="No Line" custom_height="300"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row type="full_width_background" full_screen_row_position="middle" scene_position="center" text_color="custom" text_align="left" top_padding="4%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="middle" column_margin="default" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="2/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][nectar_animated_title heading_tag="h2" style="color-strip-reveal" color="Accent-Color" text="Why is my concrete sinking?"][vc_column_text]Uneven concrete is caused by voids opening up below concrete slabs. These holes are usually caused by different types and densities of dirt being mixed during the construction process, then being placed under the pressure of concrete slabs, the ground starts to settle. These mixtures of dirt are also susceptible to erosion. Both rain and snow can seep below the concrete to wash away the lightly packed dirt, but this isn’t the most common reason. Usually, if the concrete is sinking, there is an underground water pipe that has broken and the water has washed away the looser dirt from below.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="padding-5-percent" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#f7f7f7" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" width="3/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

What can I do to fix it?

There are 2 basic repair options for uneven concrete:

  1. Removing and re-pouring concrete slabs

  2. Lifting and leveling concrete back to its original position

The first option is time-consuming, expensive, and almost impossible at some times of the year. The concrete has to be entirely broken up and carted away, then the hole needs to be filled and tamped down before it can be framed in and the new concrete can be poured. The concrete needs to cure for weeks, in mild to hot weather, undisturbed in order to cure. That’s a lot of trouble to go through for level concrete.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_column_text]

The second option is what we recommend and it only takes a few hours!

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row type="full_width_background" full_screen_row_position="middle" equal_height="yes" content_placement="bottom" scene_position="center" text_color="custom" text_align="left" top_padding="3%" color_overlay="#ffffff" overlay_strength="0.5" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/3" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_color="#F15C28" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="bottom" column_margin="none" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][image_with_animation image_url="1039" alignment="" animation="Fade In" border_radius="none" box_shadow="none" max_width="100%"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#221e1e" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text][nectar_dropcap color="#F15C28"]1[/nectar_dropcap]

DRILL

[/vc_column_text][nectar_animated_title heading_tag="h6" style="color-strip-reveal" color="Extra-Color-1" text="A pattern of dime-sized holes is drilled through the sunken concrete slabs."][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/3" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="bottom" column_margin="none" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][image_with_animation image_url="1038" alignment="" animation="Fade In" border_radius="none" box_shadow="none" max_width="100%"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#221e1e" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text][nectar_dropcap color="#F15C28"]2[/nectar_dropcap]

A void is a hole, usually caused when different densities of dirt are combined during a home's construction. When the dirt is under the pressure of concrete slabs, the ground starts to settle, especially if there has been erosion. Both rain and snow can seep below the concrete to wash away the looser packed dirt, but this isn’t usually the reason. The most common reason for the ground to settle and the ground to sink is underground water pipes that have broken. The water washes away the looser dirt right out from under the concrete.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="padding-5-percent" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#f7f7f7" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" width="3/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

What can I do to fix it?

There are 2 basic repairs for uneven concrete:

  1. Removing and re-pouring concrete slab

  2. Lifting concrete back into its original position

The first option is expensive, difficult, and time-consuming. The concrete has to be entirely broken up, and removed and the hole needs to be filled and tamped down before it can be framed in and the new concrete can be poured. The concrete will need to cure for weeks if the weather is warm enough. That’s a lot of trouble to go through for level concrete.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_column_text]

The second option is what we recommend and it only takes a few hours!

[vc_row type="full_width_background" full_screen_row_position="middle" bg_color="#221e1e" scene_position="center" video_bg="use_video" enable_video_color_overlay="true" video_overlay_color="#221e1e" video_external="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y63yGoaN9EY" text_color="light" text_align="left" top_padding="4%" bottom_padding="4%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="middle" column_margin="default" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

If you’ve stubbed your toe for the last time on your uneven concrete, Landmark Lifting is here to help.

We’re ready to handle all of your concrete lifting in Sandy, Utah, and regardless of the time of year, we’ll make your concrete driveways, patios, and walkways safer to use.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner background_image="1014" enable_bg_scale="true" column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][divider line_type="No Line" custom_height="300"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row type="full_width_background" full_screen_row_position="middle" scene_position="center" text_color="custom" text_align="left" top_padding="4%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="middle" column_margin="default" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="2/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][nectar_animated_title heading_tag="h2" style="color-strip-reveal" color="Accent-Color" text="Why is my concrete sinking?"][vc_column_text]Uneven concrete is caused by voids opening up below concrete slabs. These holes are usually caused by different types and densities of dirt being mixed during the construction process, then being placed under the pressure of concrete slabs, the ground starts to settle. These mixtures of dirt are also susceptible to erosion. Both rain and snow can seep below the concrete to wash away the lightly packed dirt, but this isn’t the most common reason. Usually, if the concrete is sinking, there is an underground water pipe that has broken and the water has washed away the looser dirt from below.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="padding-5-percent" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#f7f7f7" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" width="3/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

What can I do to fix it?

There are 2 basic repair options for uneven concrete:

  1. Removing and re-pouring concrete slabs

  2. Lifting and leveling concrete back to its original position

The first option is time-consuming, expensive, and almost impossible at some times of the year. The concrete has to be entirely broken up and carted away, then the hole needs to be filled and tamped down before it can be framed in and the new concrete can be poured. The concrete needs to cure for weeks, in mild to hot weather, undisturbed in order to cure. That’s a lot of trouble to go through for level concrete.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_column_text]

The second option is what we recommend and it only takes a few hours!

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row type="full_width_background" full_screen_row_position="middle" equal_height="yes" content_placement="bottom" scene_position="center" text_color="custom" text_align="left" top_padding="3%" color_overlay="#ffffff" overlay_strength="0.5" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/3" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_color="#F15C28" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="bottom" column_margin="none" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][image_with_animation image_url="1039" alignment="" animation="Fade In" border_radius="none" box_shadow="none" max_width="100%"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#221e1e" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text][nectar_dropcap color="#F15C28"]1[/nectar_dropcap]

DRILL

[/vc_column_text][nectar_animated_title heading_tag="h6" style="color-strip-reveal" color="Extra-Color-1" text="A pattern of dime-sized holes is drilled through the sunken concrete slabs."][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/3" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="bottom" column_margin="none" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][image_with_animation image_url="1038" alignment="" animation="Fade In" border_radius="none" box_shadow="none" max_width="100%"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#221e1e" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text][nectar_dropcap color="#F15C28"]2[/nectar_dropcap]

LIFT

content:
[vc_row type="full_width_background" full_screen_row_position="middle" bg_color="#221e1e" scene_position="center" video_bg="use_video" enable_video_color_overlay="true" video_overlay_color="#221e1e" video_external="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y63yGoaN9EY" text_color="light" text_align="left" top_padding="4%" bottom_padding="4%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="middle" column_margin="default" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

If you’ve stubbed your toe for the last time on your uneven concrete, Landmark Lifting is here to help.

We’re ready to handle all of your concrete lifting in Solitude, Utah, and regardless of the time of year, we’ll make your concrete driveways, patios, and walkways safer to use.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner background_image="1014" enable_bg_scale="true" column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][divider line_type="No Line" custom_height="300"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row type="full_width_background" full_screen_row_position="middle" scene_position="center" text_color="custom" text_align="left" top_padding="4%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="middle" column_margin="default" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="2/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][nectar_animated_title heading_tag="h2" style="color-strip-reveal" color="Accent-Color" text="Why is my concrete sinking?"][vc_column_text]Uneven concrete is caused by voids opening up below concrete slabs. These holes are usually caused by different types and densities of dirt being mixed during the construction process, then being placed under the pressure of concrete slabs, the ground starts to settle. These mixtures of dirt are also susceptible to erosion. Both rain and snow can seep below the concrete to wash away the lightly packed dirt, but this isn’t the most common reason. Usually, if the concrete is sinking, there is an underground water pipe that has broken and the water has washed away the looser dirt from below.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="padding-5-percent" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#f7f7f7" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" width="3/5" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

What can I do to fix it?

There are 2 basic repair options for uneven concrete:

  1. Removing and re-pouring concrete slabs

  2. Lifting and leveling concrete back to its original position

The first option is time-consuming, expensive, and almost impossible at some times of the year. The concrete has to be entirely broken up and carted away, then the hole needs to be filled and tamped down before it can be framed in and the new concrete can be poured. The concrete needs to cure for weeks, in mild to hot weather, undisturbed in order to cure. That’s a lot of trouble to go through for level concrete.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_column_text]

The second option is what we recommend and it only takes a few hours!

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row type="full_width_background" full_screen_row_position="middle" equal_height="yes" content_placement="bottom" scene_position="center" text_color="custom" text_align="left" top_padding="3%" color_overlay="#ffffff" overlay_strength="0.5" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/3" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_color="#F15C28" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="bottom" column_margin="none" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][image_with_animation image_url="1039" alignment="" animation="Fade In" border_radius="none" box_shadow="none" max_width="100%"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#221e1e" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text][nectar_dropcap color="#F15C28"]1[/nectar_dropcap]

DRILL

[/vc_column_text][nectar_animated_title heading_tag="h6" style="color-strip-reveal" color="Extra-Color-1" text="A pattern of dime-sized holes is drilled through the sunken concrete slabs."][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/3" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_row_inner equal_height="yes" content_placement="bottom" column_margin="none" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][image_with_animation image_url="1038" alignment="" animation="Fade In" border_radius="none" box_shadow="none" max_width="100%"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#221e1e" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text][nectar_dropcap color="#F15C28"]2[/nectar_dropcap]

LIFT
