css=""][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Water damage isn't always obvious at first. Here are a few warning signs to watch for:
  • Cracking or crumbling concrete: Surface cracks can indicate that water has entered the slab and is compromising its structure from within.
  • Pooling water or soggy soil: Water that doesn't drain properly around walkways, driveways, or foundations can quickly lead to slab shifting or settlement.
  • Discoloration or efflorescence: White, chalky residue on your concrete can be a sign of water moving through the material and bringing salts to the surface.
  • Sinking or uneven slabs: As water erodes the soil underneath your concrete, it creates voids that lead to uneven or sunken surfaces.
If you notice any of these issues, it's important to address them sooner rather than later. Delaying repairs can result in more extensive (and expensive) damage.[/vc_column_text][nectar_btn size="jumbo" button_style="regular" button_color_2="Accent-Color" icon_family="none" css=""][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]The best defense against water damage is proper drainage and regular maintenance. Here are a few steps homeowners can take to minimize water intrusion:
  • Keep gutters and downspouts clear and functioning: Ensure they direct water away from your home and concrete surfaces.
  • Regrade landscaping if necessary: Make sure the slope directs water away from structures, not toward them.
  • Seal your concrete: A high-quality sealer can help reduce water absorption, especially on exposed surfaces like driveways and patios.
  • Repair cracks quickly: Small cracks are an open door for water. Sealing them early can prevent more significant issues down the road.

title: Is Your Concrete a Trip Hazard?
content:
[vc_row type="in_container" full_screen_row_position="middle" scene_position="center" text_color="dark" text_align="left" top_padding="3%" bottom_padding="2%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="padding-3-percent" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#221e1e" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" font_color="#ffffff" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" width="1/3" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none"][vc_column_text]

How worried do you need to be about trip hazards in your concrete?

Most people know if there is a trip hazard in their yard after you catch your toe once on a piece of uneven paving or concrete, you remember it; even toddlers remember and can watch out for trip hazards they’ve fallen over in the past. A trip hazard is technically any portion of the ground that is not level, anything a person can trip over.[/vc_column_text][nectar_image_comparison image_url="1191" image_2_url="1192"][nectar_image_comparison image_url="1129" image_2_url="1128"][/vc_column][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="2/3" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

Legal Definition & Ramifications of a Trip Hazard

Did you know that there was a legal definition of a trip hazard? Legally, anything greater than a quarter of an inch can be considered a trip hazard. If you own the property with an offending trip hazard on the property, you can be held liable for injuries caused and medical costs incurred by victims. I know, it’s not a pleasant thought, but it’s better to be safe than sorry.[/vc_column_text][vc_gallery type="image_grid" images="1182,1179,1180" layout="3" gallery_style="1" load_in_animation="none"][vc_column_text]

Trip Hazard Repair

The best, fastest and most affordable way to get rid of a trip hazard on your walkway, driveway or other concrete surface is concrete leveling. We start by identifying the placement of the cavity or “void” beneath your concrete, and then we:
  • Drill a dime-sized (⅝”) hole in your concrete
  • Insert an air-tight tube
  • Attach a hose from our pressurized injection system to the tube
  • Inject our eco-friendly polyurethane expanding foam
  • Remove the tube
  • Patch the dime-sized hole
[/vc_column_text][vc_row_inner column_margin="default" text_align="left"][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/4" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][image_with_animation image_url="1039" alignment="" animation="Fade In" border_radius="none" box_shadow="none" max_width="100%"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/4" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][image_with_animation image_url="1038" alignment="" animation="Fade In" border_radius="none" box_shadow="none" max_width="100%"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/4" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][image_with_animation image_url="1037" alignment="" animation="Fade In" border_radius="none" box_shadow="none" max_width="100%"][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" width="1/4" tablet_width_inherit="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][vc_column_text]Our work can be finished in as little as 30 minutes and will be fully cured within minutes after we’re done and can even be driven on at that point! This is a simple and effective solution to voids and trip hazards. The alternative, on the other hand, is expensive, time-consuming and aggravating; the alternative is replacing your concrete. Replacing concrete starts with several days of demolition, cleanup, placing and packing new dirt and finally pouring the concrete. After that, you get to wait up to 2-3 months for it to finally finish curing to the point that it can take weight without marring. Finally and most importantly, replacing your concrete slab will cost you twice as much as it costs to lift your concrete. The solution is clear, call Landmark Lifting to help you repair your concrete toe catchers before they have a chance to hurt anyone.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row type="in_container" full_screen_row_position="middle" scene_position="center" text_color="dark" text_align="left" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom"][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text][ls_content_block id="1071"][/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]

concrete?"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Voids in concrete can form due to several factors, including soil erosion, poor drainage, and settlement of the underlying soil. Other causes may include shifting ground due to freeze-thaw cycles, tree root growth, or excavation activities nearby. Over time, these conditions can create air pockets or cavities beneath the concrete slab, leading to uneven surfaces.[/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color="Default" heading_tag="h4" heading_tag_functionality="default" title="What are the potential consequences of leaving voids unfilled?"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Leaving voids unfilled can lead to serious issues, including further settling or sinking of the concrete slab, which can result in cracks and structural damage. This can create tripping hazards, reduce the lifespan of the concrete, and compromise the safety and aesthetics of the surface. Additionally, unaddressed voids may allow water to accumulate, leading to further erosion and degradation of the surrounding soil.[/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color="Default" heading_tag="h4" heading_tag_functionality="default" title="How can I identify if there are voids in my concrete?"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]You can identify voids in your concrete by looking for signs such as visible cracks, uneven surfaces, or depressions. If you notice areas where the concrete feels unstable or produces a hollow sound when tapped, these may indicate the presence of voids. [/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color="Default" heading_tag="h4" heading_tag_functionality="default" title="How long will the results of void filling last?"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]The results of void filling can be quite durable, often lasting for many years if the underlying issues are addressed and properly managed. However, factors such as soil conditions, moisture levels, and heavy traffic can impact the longevity of the results. It's important to monitor the concrete surface for any signs of settling or new voids, as prompt action can help maintain the effectiveness of the void filling service over time.[/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color="Default" heading_tag="h4" heading_tag_functionality="default" title="Are there any preparations I need to make before the void filling service?"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Before the void filling service, it’s important to clear the area of any furniture, vehicles, or obstacles that may hinder access to the concrete surfaces being treated. You should also ensure that any landscaping or vegetation near the area is trimmed back to allow for adequate working space. Providing quick, cost-effective concrete lifting is what we do

We can save you half the cost of removing and replacing your concrete, and we can do it in minutes instead of months!

Have you got an uneven slab of concrete? Traditionally, fixing a sunken piece of concrete involves removing and replacing the slab, but that's not what we do. That process involves:

  • Breaking the concrete up into pieces with sledgehammers
  • Hauling the pieces to the dump
  • Filling the void with dirt
  • Packing the dirt tightly and leveling it
  • Building the frame for the concrete to be poured into
  • Pouring the new concrete slab
  • Waiting for a few weeks/months for the concrete to cure fully, to be able to support weight.

When compared to concrete replacement, the process of raising concrete with Landmark Lifting's polyurethane foam is fast, convenient, inexpensive and effective. Once we've repaired an area, the slab will be ready within minutes to be walked on, driven across or even parked on, as it was originally intended. Raising concrete with polyurethane foam is done with incremental injections. Lifting foam will fully expand within 10-15 seconds allowing you to monitor the raising and preventing over raising the slab.

  1. A ⅝” hole is drilled through the slab into the subgrade
  2. A tapered delivery port is inserted into the ⅝” hole
    • Our polyurethane foam injection method uses the concrete slab itself as a means of delivering poly foams that raises concrete, fills voids, and stabilizes the soil.
  3. The injection gun attaches directly to the port inserted into the concrete slab
    • The injection gun then delivers the polyurethane mixture through the port and slab and into the void below the slab itself.
  4. The expansion of the materials occurs within seconds, compressing loose soils and raising the concrete

Raising concrete with polyurethane foam is done with incremental injections. The lifting foam will fully expand within 10-15 seconds allowing you to monitor the raising and preventing over raising the slab. The resulting foam will solidify, or cure, within 15 minutes and then it will be strong enough to support several thousand pounds per square foot.

The ease of use with our polyurethane material makes our process easy to use, fast and easy to clean-up, which are some distinct advantages over other methods of concrete repair or replacement companies.

Lifting uneven concrete is what we do and we're the best at it. If you've got a problem with your concrete, give us a call before it gets any worse and we'll save you the time, inconvenience and money of removing and replacing your concrete.

title: When to Lift Concrete
content:
[vc_row type="in_container" full_screen_row_position="middle" column_margin="default" equal_height="yes" content_placement="middle" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" scene_position="center" top_padding="3%" bottom_padding="2%" text_color="dark" text_align="left" row_border_radius="none" row_border_radius_applies="bg" overflow="visible" overlay_strength="0.3" gradient_direction="left_to_right" shape_divider_position="bottom" bg_image_animation="none" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="padding-3-percent" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color="#221e1e" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" font_color="#ffffff" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" column_link_target="_self" column_position="default" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/3" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][nectar_image_comparison image_url="1179" image_2_url="1178"][vc_custom_heading text="Landmark Lifting" font_container="tag:h3|text_align:left" use_theme_fonts="yes" css=""][vc_column_text]Knowing when to lift concrete isn’t that difficult; there’s no telling when or if concrete will shift and it may never move, but if it does it’ll need to be lifted. The most important rule about concrete is that it’s only as good as the material underneath it.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column column_padding="padding-2-percent" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" column_position="default" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="2/3" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid" column_padding_type="default" gradient_type="default"][vc_custom_heading text="KNOWING WHEN TO LIFT CONCRETE AND THE COMMON CAUSES OF CONCRETE DAMAGE." use_theme_fonts="yes" css=""][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]Concrete is a strong, durable material, but it relies heavily on the stability of the ground beneath it. Over time, shifting or settling soil can cause concrete to crack, sink, or become uneven. Recognizing when it’s time to lift concrete is crucial in preventing further damage and maintaining safety. There are a variety of factors that can cause concrete to become unstable. Understanding these issues helps homeowners and business owners make informed decisions about when to take action.

Concrete damage doesn’t always happen overnight. It can take years for the subtle effects of settling or water damage to become noticeable. However, recognizing the signs early on can help prevent more extensive damage later. Among the most common causes of concrete shifting are house settling and water damage. Understanding these causes is essential for knowing when to lift concrete, and knowing when to act will help you avoid unnecessary repair costs.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column House Settling

When new homes are being built, there are a number of underground excavations, especially for laying pipes. When an excavator is backfilling the water and sewer trenches around the foundation, it is important that he uses the right amount of water and compaction, bringing it up in lifts so that it is tight going back into the trench. This will prevent it from settling into voids in the future. A house will typically settle for about the first 10 years, beyond that, settling problems will be few and far between.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" overflow="visible" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/2" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]

Water Damage

If water saturates the ground beneath a concrete slab, the dirt will lose its tension and start to wash away. Unfortunately, this is usually invisible from the surface, because it’s almost always caused by one of the previously mentioned pipes breaking, under a concrete slab. Slabs that are settling or sinking into the ground need to be lifted back into their original position before they become trip hazards and cause injuries, or start to crack and break concrete damage. Some early indicators include:

  • Uneven concrete surfaces: If certain areas of your concrete appear to be sinking or tilting, it’s a clear sign that the foundation underneath is unstable.
  • Cracks in the surface: Cracks that develop in concrete slabs, walls, or foundations are often caused by shifting or settling. If you notice cracks, it’s time to investigate further.
  • Pooling water: Water that collects in certain areas, particularly where it didn’t collect before, can be a result of the concrete becoming uneven and causing drainage issues.
  • Gaps between concrete slabs: If gaps form between concrete slabs or between slabs and walls, it’s likely that the concrete has shifted or sunk beneath the surface.
  • Doors or windows sticking: Misalignment of doors or windows can occur when the foundation shifts. If doors and windows no longer open or close properly, it may indicate a problem with the concrete.

If you’re noticing any of these signs, don’t wait until the problem becomes more serious. Acting quickly to know if you should lift the concrete back into place can prevent further damage and protect your property.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][vc_column title: Why Does Concrete Crack?
content:
[vc_row type="in_container" full_screen_row_position="middle" scene_position="center" text_color="dark" text_align="left" top_padding="3%" bottom_padding="2%" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom" shape_type=""][vc_column column_padding="padding-3-percent" column_padding_position="all" background_color="#221e1e" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" font_color="#ffffff" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="5px" width="1/3" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none"][nectar_image_comparison image_url="1014" image_2_url="1013"][vc_column_text]

You’ve invested years of your income, time and labor into purchasing and caring for your home, the least it can do is remain in one piece!

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="2/3" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text]

Why Do Houses Settle and Why Does Concrete Crack?

Congratulations, you're a homeowner and you’re enjoying your little piece of the American Dream. The unspoken downside of owning your home is that when things go wrong, you’re the one who has to figure out how to fix it. That means that when the ground literally drops out from under you, you need to figure out why and what you can possibly do to fix it. So, why does concrete crack? Whether in your driveway, walkway, patio, porch or garage, your concrete is only as good as the material underneath it and if it changes shape, concrete won’t bend, it’ll crack and or fall into the indent. Concrete slabs are created with joints spaced out to prevent cracking. These weak points allow concrete to crack in a clean line with a tapered top if the slab was properly scored with “joints”. If that is the case, all we’ll need to do is fill the void beneath the concrete with our eco-friendly polyurethane expanding foam, and the slab will rise back into place. If you’re not this lucky, the concrete will break jaggedly, somewhere in the middle of the slab. This can still be fixed, but it won’t be as pretty. In these cases, the sooner you call us the better because as they are bumped and tripped over, pieces will chip away and the surface won’t look as clean when the work is eventually done. When we come out we’ll need to fill the crack with SikaFlex, to ensure that we stop moisture from seeping in and expanding the crack further. Because we live in Utah, with a constant annual cycle of freezing and thawing, rain and snow, our concrete is always at risk of water seeping into cracks, freezing, expanding, cracking the concrete and repeating again and again. Once the crack has broken through to the ground, the moisture creates soft spots, erosion, and settling, leading to more cracks and lifting projects. Regardless of where your concrete has cracked, we can come out and fill the void, lift the concrete, seal the cracks and or joints to keep the moisture out. Give us a call and reclaim your smooth walkway.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row type="in_container" full_screen_row_position="middle" scene_position="center" text_color="dark" text_align="left" overlay_strength="0.3" shape_divider_position="bottom"][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_position="all" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_link_target="_self" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text][ls_content_block id="1071"][/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]

content:

At Landmark Lifting, we get this same question asked in every possible way, people know that they have a problem, but not sure what the best solution is for them.

[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" column_position="default" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="2/3" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text css="" text_direction="default"]

Why lift concrete instead of replacing it?

At Landmark Lifting, we lift concrete with a special polyurethane foam. Here are some signs that you should lift your concrete instead of removing and replacing it:

  1. Your walkway or driveway has settled and is sinking into the ground.
  2. You hear a hollow sound under your concrete when you walk across your patio or bounce a ball on it.
  3. Your concrete has cracked and is falling into a void.
  4. Your concrete is in any way uneven potentially causing a trip hazard.

If you have any of these symptoms, you’re suffering from a void under your concrete and the prescription is lifting your concrete. The alternative, breaking the concrete, removing it, taking it to the dump and pouring a new slab of concrete is extreme and should only be used in extreme cases. It is also extremely time-consuming, expensive and frustrating.

The differences between replacing and raising your concrete

The differences between replacing and lifting your concrete back into place are simple but important. When we can lift your concrete into place, we can do it in as little as 45 minutes. On the other hand, if you replace your concrete, it takes days to go through the demo and construction of repouring your concrete. This is often followed by weeks, if not months, without being able to drive on it.
When we lift concrete with our polyurethane foam, it cures within 15 minutes and can be used immediately after we’re done. Most importantly for our customers, re-pouring concrete slabs usually cost 2x more than it costs to lift them back into place.

If you’ve got a slab that’s sinking into the ground, give us a call today and we’ll come and take care of it in no time.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row type="in_container" full_screen_row_position="middle" column_margin="default" column_direction="default" column_direction_tablet="default" column_direction_phone="default" scene_position="center" text_color="dark" text_align="left" row_border_radius="none" row_border_radius_applies="bg" overflow="visible" overlay_strength="0.3" gradient_direction="left_to_right" shape_divider_position="bottom" bg_image_animation="none"][vc_column column_padding="no-extra-padding" column_padding_tablet="inherit" column_padding_phone="inherit" column_padding_position="all" column_element_direction_desktop="default" column_element_spacing="default" desktop_text_alignment="default" tablet_text_alignment="default" phone_text_alignment="default" background_color_opacity="1" background_hover_color_opacity="1" column_backdrop_filter="none" column_shadow="none" column_border_radius="none" column_link_target="_self" column_position="default" gradient_direction="left_to_right" overlay_strength="0.3" width="1/1" tablet_width_inherit="default" animation_type="default" bg_image_animation="none" border_type="simple" column_border_width="none" column_border_style="solid"][vc_column_text][ls_content_block id="1071"][/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]

title: A Word From Our Owner
content:
As I have been operating the concrete lifting business over the past several years now, concrete replacement and placing new concrete is something that comes up regularly, maybe every day. I have attempted in the past to include it, having guys I know do the work so I can be a one-stop shop for my customers. For me, it never felt right because I didn't like not being in control over the schedule of people who didn't actually work for me. If a guy didn't show up or didn't do the quality work I had expected it was also a direct reflection on me as well, which was too much for me to stomach. About a year ago I slowly and organically built a relationship with a group of guys that do concrete work at a high level. They are very professional and think like I do. They spend most of their time doing commercial and high-end residential work on several of the homes featured in Parade Of Homes. I liked this as those jobs often require the highest level of expertise and quality. I did a job or two with them and tested the waters if you will. Slowly we have done more and more and the consistency has been great! So, why not just call these guys or any other concrete company and work with them directly and save money? This is one of my main hurdles as I went into this. I wanted to make sure my pricing was still competitive. The advantage for them is they don't have to sell as I arrange and manage the project, while they just have to come in and do the work. This way, I get pricing that is competitive with any other company. I always tell my customers to get other bids as well so they can make the right decision. Price is one aspect of making a decision on who to hire to do work at your home. Other factors that are important include the following:
  • Do they show up to give a bid and do the work?
  • Is the price reasonable?
  • Can you work with their personality and are they someone you want to work with?
  • Are they trustworthy?
  • Do you think they will get you to the finish line on the project and stand behind the work?
These are all things on the concrete lifting side of the business that have propelled us to where we are today, and we fully intend to extend each of those things as we incorporate concrete installation, removal, and replacement. Our customers appreciate the education they get along the way and the communication from beginning to end. I hope this personal message finds you well and gives an explanation of how we are operating our concrete division at Landmark Lifting in Utah. The economy is pretty crazy, it is hard to get a contractor to call you back, and even harder to find one that will come out and do a good job, and a clean job and image at that! That is my goal in what we are trying to provide.

title: Beyond the Band-Aid: Why Proper Concrete Patching Matters
content:
Cracks, potholes, and crumbling edges in your concrete can be more than just eyesores; they can be trip hazards, entry points for water, and signs of deeper underlying issues. While it might be tempting to just "slap a band-aid" on the problem, proper concrete patching is a critical skill that, when done correctly, can significantly extend the life of your concrete surfaces and prevent minor issues from becoming major headaches.

But when is patching the right solution, and why does doing it right truly matter?

Is Patching the Right Solution for Your Concrete?

Not all concrete damage is created equal, and understanding when patching is appropriate is key. Patching is generally effective for:

  • Surface Spalling and Chipping: This occurs when the top layer of concrete flakes or peels off, often due to freeze-thaw cycles, de-icing salts, or poor finishing. Patching can restore the surface integrity.
  • Minor Cracks: Hairline cracks or those that aren't actively expanding can often be successfully patched, especially on non-structural elements like driveways or patios.
  • Potholes and Divots: These can form from heavy impact, poor drainage, or freeze-thaw damage. Patching restores a smooth, safe surface.
  • Damaged Edges and Corners: Chipped or broken edges on steps, curbs, or slabs can be repaired to improve safety and appearance.
  • Aesthetic Repair: When the damage is primarily cosmetic and doesn't compromise the structural integrity.

When is patching NOT enough? If you're dealing with wide, deep, or actively spreading cracks, significant settling, severe structural damage, or extensive network cracking (alligator cracking), patching might only be a temporary fix. In these cases, it's crucial to consult with a concrete professional like Landmark Lifting to assess whether more extensive repair or replacement is needed.

Why "Doing It Right" Matters: The Risks of DIY Patching

It's easy to grab a bucket of patching compound from the hardware store, but true, lasting concrete repair is more complex than it appears. Poorly executed patches can lead to:

Poor Adhesion

If the surface isn't properly prepared, the patch won't bond effectively to the existing concrete. This leads to the patch delaminating, cracking, or simply popping out after a short time.

Inconsistent Durability

Different patching materials have varying strengths and flexibilities. Using the wrong material for the job can result in a patch that's either too rigid and cracks, or too soft and wears away quickly.

Color Mismatch

Achieving a seamless look is challenging. A poorly matched patch stands out, making the repair obvious and often less appealing than the original damage.

Water Intrusion

An improperly applied patch can still allow water to seep underneath or around it, continuing the destructive cycle of freeze-thaw and rebar corrosion.

Temporary Fixes

Without understanding the root cause of the damage (e.g., poor drainage, sub-base issues), a DIY patch is often just a temporary band-aid that will fail again.

The Benefits of Professional Concrete Patching

When done correctly by experienced professionals, concrete patching offers significant benefits:

  • Extended Lifespan: A properly prepared and applied patch can significantly prolong the life of your existing concrete, delaying the need for costly replacement.
  • Enhanced Safety: Eliminating trip hazards from cracks and potholes makes your property safer for family, visitors, and customers.
  • Improved Aesthetics: Expertly matched and finished patches blend seamlessly, restoring the curb appeal of your driveways, patios, and walkways.
  • Preventative Maintenance: Sealing off damaged areas prevents water from exacerbating existing problems and causing new ones.
  • Cost-Effective Solution: Patching is generally far more affordable than full concrete replacement, offering an excellent return on investment.

Don't let concrete damage detract from your property's safety or appearance. If you have cracked, chipped, or spalled concrete, reach out to Landmark Lifting a professional assessment. A well-executed patch isn't just a band-aid; it's a strategic repair that protects your investment for years to come.

title: CS Concrete Densifier: Strengthen, Protect, and Enhance Your Concrete with Landmark Lifting
content:
Unlock the true potential of your concrete surfaces with CS Concrete Densifier from Landmark Lifting the ultimate solution for stronger floors, reduced dusting, and long-lasting protection.

If you’re frustrated with concrete surfaces that wear down quickly, chip, or stain easily, you’re not alone. Whether it’s a driveway, garage, warehouse, workshop, retail space, or basement, untreated concrete is porous and vulnerable to damage. The CS Concrete Densifier is designed to transform bare concrete into a harder, denser, and more resilient surface that can withstand heavy use for years to come.

What is CS Concrete Densifier?

The CS Concrete Densifier is a high-performance, water-based solution that penetrates deeply into concrete surfaces. Through a chemical reaction, it hardens and densifies the concrete, improving resistance to abrasion, dusting, and moisture. This makes it an essential treatment for maximizing the durability and performance of concrete floors in both residential and commercial settings.

Why Choose CS Concrete Densifier from Landmark Lifting?

  • Superior Hardness & Durability – Strengthens weak or soft concrete into a denser, more robust surface resistant to heavy wear, chipping, and abrasion.
  • Dust-Free Finish – Binds free lime and particles inside the concrete, virtually eliminating dusty footprints and constant cleaning.
  • Stain Resistance – Reduces porosity, helping protect against oil, grease, and chemical spills.
  • Enhanced Appearance – Creates a smoother, refined surface that develops a subtle sheen with use, elevating the look of your concrete.
  • Perfect for Future Treatments – Provides a reliable foundation for polishing, staining, or sealing, ensuring long-lasting results.
  • Easy, Eco-Friendly Application – Low-VOC, water-based, and safe for use in homes, businesses, and industrial facilities.

Best Applications for CS Concrete Densifier

Landmark Lifting recommends CS Concrete Densifier for a variety of surfaces, including:

  • Garage Floors – Protection against car traffic, oil, and spills.
  • Warehouses & Industrial Facilities – Added strength for forklifts, machinery, and foot traffic.
  • Workshops & Basements – Cleaner, dust-free work areas.
  • Retail Spaces – Improved durability in high-traffic customer environments.
  • Driveways & Patios – Resistance to weathering and outdoor abrasion.
  • Concrete Countertops – Added protection against stains and daily use.

How Does CS Concrete Densifier Work?

When applied, the silicates in the densifier react with calcium hydroxide in the concrete to form Calcium Silicate Hydrate (CSH) – the same compound responsible for concrete’s natural strength. By filling in the pores, the densifier makes the surface denser, harder, and more resistant to wear and moisture.

Simple Application Process

  1. Surface Prep – Clean and dry the concrete; repair cracks or damaged areas.
  2. Apply Evenly – Use a low-pressure sprayer, brush, or roller to coat the surface.
  3. Keep Wet – Maintain a wet surface for 20–30 minutes, scrubbing gently to ensure penetration.
  4. Rinse & Remove Residue – Rinse thoroughly after the reaction period.
  5. Allow to Cure – Let the surface dry; full densification develops over several days.

At Landmark Lifting, we specialize in concrete lifting, repair, and protection solutions. By incorporating CS Concrete Densifier into your project, you can extend the life of your floors, prevent dusting, and create a cleaner, more resilient surface.

title: How Much Polyurethane Does it Take to Lift Concrete?
content:
How much polyurethane does it take to lift concrete slabs in sidewalks and driveways?

We're often asked "how much polyurethane does it take to lift concrete?" We can estimate how much it will take to get your concrete lifted back to its original position, but we have to take a few things into consideration.

When is it necessary to lift concrete?

Our polyurethane foam is a two-part expanding chemical combination that, when combined, creates a chemical reaction that generates heat and expands into a foam, strong enough to lift and hold concrete slabs. Our polyurethane mixture can be used to fill voids under concrete slabs where the ground has settled. If your concrete is sinking into a void, we can inject this material into it to lift the slab until your concrete is level again.

How we estimate the amount of polyurethane it takes to level your concrete

In order to estimate how much polyurethane it will take to lift and level your concrete slab, we actually find out how many cubic yards of dirt is missing, underground, which our material will be replacing. So, if it is a 10' x 10' concrete slab in your driveway and it has settled on two sides 1 inch it will take .23 cubic yards of material to get the slab lifted.

The difference between Mud Jacking and Polyurethane concrete lifting

In our industry, there are 2 main competitors, Mud jacking and our polyurethane lifting services. Mud jacking contractors charge by the cubic yard of material they inject into a void and polyurethane contractors charge per pound of material which is converted from cubic yards. The reason for this is that polyurethane foam is purchased by the pound in liquid form.

How we know the size of underground voids

A question often asked at the time of the estimate is "how do you know how big the void is under the slab?" We look for signs of voids the best we can by looking at the side of the slab to see if we can see gaps and we also check to see if it sounds hollow under the concrete; that is good indication of a void. It can be hard to tell how deep the void goes though, so instead of guessing we like to drill a very small hole in the joint (where it will be inconspicuous, even when we patch it) and putting a stick down to measure the distance to the dirt. This is the most fool-proof way to find out how much foam compound it will take to fill the void.

Why polyurethane foam is a better solution to your underground void

After answering "how much polyurethane does it take to lift concrete" the next question is usually "why not remove and replace the concrete?" Some of the advantages of having your void filled with polyurethane foam rather than removing and replacing the slab are that we can save lots of time and money. The price of concrete lifting seems expensive at the time but when you think about the alternative it is half the cost or less, of the alternatives. When you remove your concrete to fill a void, you will have to:
  1. Spend a full day of removing concrete and hauling it off to a place that accepts concrete, which usually comes with a price tag of its own.
  2. The next step is to compact the dirt in the bottom of the void and bring more dirt in, to get it back to the proper grade so that a new slab can be placed.
  3. The concrete contractor has to set forms for the new concrete and a big concrete mixer has to come and place the concrete.
  4. The contractor has to finish the concrete then come back a day or two later and strip the forms.
  5. You'll then need some landscape restoration performed where they had to set their forms.
  6. You'll have to wait to drive on the concrete for a week, and it won't match any of the concrete around it.
The bottom line is that you are typically down for about a week at least, the cost is astronomical, and there is a much better way to resolve your problem. Concrete lifting, concrete leveling, and void filling can come in handy in these instances. So, to answer your question, "how much polyurethane does it take to lift concrete" it varies; but it takes less material than the alternatives and it costs less. Our jobs typically take about 2 hours, and you can drive on your concrete again immediately after the work is complete.

title: Is Your Backyard Oasis Sinking? The Real Reason Utah Patios Crack and How to Fix It
content:
There is nothing quite like enjoying a warm Utah evening out on your back patio, grilling with family and looking up at the mountains. But if you’re constantly stubbing your toes on an uneven concrete slab or looking down at ugly, gaping cracks, that backyard retreat doesn’t feel like much of an oasis. When homeowners see their patio sinking, they usually stress, thinking they have to tear the whole thing out and start over. But as we like to tell our customers here at Landmark Lifting, We can make two promises about concrete: Number one is that it will crack, and number two is that no one is going to steal it. The trick isn’t expecting concrete to be perfect forever; it's knowing how to take care of it when it moves.

The Real Culprit: It’s What’s Underneath Your Patio That Counts

The truth is, your concrete is only as good as the material underneath it. Here in Utah, we deal with a lot of settled and shifted ground. Much of our local soil was basically "terraformed" years ago, mixing dirt of different densities that settle naturally over time under the weight of a slab. If you live in a newer home, especially one built in the last five years, settling is highly common as the loose backfill around your foundation slowly packs down. Most of our calls for settling issues come from homes in that one-to-five-year window. But soil density isn't the only issue. The real "hidden enemy" of your patio is water. When water sheets off your roof or patio, if you have a broken sprinkler pipe, or if your rain gutters dump water right next to the slab, it creates underground channels. That water washes away the supporting dirt, leaving empty cavities, or voids, beneath the surface. Eventually, the heavy concrete loses support and cracks, settling right into the void.

The Big Mistake: Slapping a Band-Aid on a Sinking Slab

When these cracks appear, many homeowners run to the hardware store, grab a bucket of concrete patch, and try to slap a quick fix over the cracks. We see DIY repair attempts about 20% to 30% of the time, and unfortunately, they fail almost 100% of the time because the underlying void isn't addressed. A surface patch is just a temporary Band-Aid. If there is an empty void underneath your patio, a cosmetic patch won't stop the slab from continuing to sink. Even worse, rigid DIY patches don't bond long-term, crack under Utah's extreme freeze-thaw cycles, and can trap water underneath, causing the surface to flake. Need a hand looking at your patio? Don't let a sinking slab paint you into a corner where a cheap fix turns into a massive replacement project. Contact us and schedule a free patio assessment with Landmark Lifting today!

The Landmark Lifting Solution: Lift It and Seal It

Instead of tearing out your concrete, a loud, messy, and expensive hassle that can cost twice as much, a smarter move is usually to have the concrete lifted. At Landmark Lifting, we use a state-of-the-art polyurethane foam injection process to save your patio:
  1. Drill: We drill a few small, dime-sized (5/8") holes in the sunken sections.
  2. Lift: We inject our eco-friendly, expanding polyurethane foam beneath the slab.
  3. Patch: The foam expands rapidly, fills the underlying voids, and gently lifts your patio back to its original level. We then patch the tiny holes with concrete, and it's ready to walk on in just 15 minutes!
Our polyurethane foam is water-resistant, made from 40% recycled materials, and will last as long as the concrete itself. Now, if your concrete is badly broken into tiny "spiderweb" pieces, lifting might not work, and a full concrete replacement is required. As a true one-stop shop for our customers, we handle both! If replacement is inevitable, we'll demo the old patio, haul it away, prepare a rock-solid compacted road base, and pour a brand new slab that matches your yard perfectly.

Stop Waiting and Restore Your Peace of Mind

Our best advice to any property owner in Salem, Spanish Fork, or Salt Lake is simple: Stay on top of it. Catching a void early might mean a quick, inexpensive lift or a simple professional caulking job to keep water out. If you wait, that simple fix can turn into a major replacement project costing thousands. Don't wait for the next freeze-thaw cycle to do more damage. Contact Landmark Lifting today to schedule your free estimate and get your backyard back on solid ground!

title: Repair Concrete Shifting
content:
If the winter has caused your concrete to shift, you need to call Steve Idol, with Landmark Lifting. Winter snow can have a big impact on the stability of concrete slabs and sidewalks. It can:
  • Saturates the soil under and around concrete with water
  • Insulates the ground, keeping the moisture in
  • Makes the wet soil shift and settle under the weight of the concrete
When voids or cavities form under concrete, concrete slabs begin to sink into them, sometimes cracking under their unsupported weight and tipping into the ground.

How can you repair concrete shifting?

Before the concrete sinks or slips too far into the ground, we can come out and fill the void with our two-part expanding foam mixture, which will fill the void and lift the concrete back to its original position. Our polyurethane foam is Eco-friendly and will not leach chemicals into the ground or groundwater. It sets up in about 15 minutes and can be driven on immediately afterward. The alternative to a few hours of our work and 15minutes of wait time is a week of demo and construction and 1-2 months of treading softly for new concrete to cure entirely. That method includes:
  1. Breaking up the concrete into small pieces
  2. Carting the pieces to the dump
  3. Filling the void with dirt and compacting the dirt
  4. Framing around the area to be poured
  5. Pouring new concrete
  6. Waiting for weeks before putting weight on the new concrete
  7. Finally being able to drive and park on it after well over a month

Do you have a void below your concrete?

Keep an eye on your concrete while you're walking around your property and you should be able to see the signs of a void. Are there any uneven sections of concrete? Can you see a black space in the crack between two adjoining concrete slabs? can you see any voids from the side of any of your concrete? Check your downspouts, if they're running with water, there is moisture in the ground. If you think you see any of these signs, give us a call and we'll come and take care of your problem for you.

title: Why Your Sidewalk Slab is Sinking
content:
Your Sidewalk Slab is Sinking, Here’s Why

You’ve got a beautiful home, an immaculate yard… and a section of sidewalk slowly sinking into it.

If you have a concrete sidewalk, walkway, or path in your front yard, there is always a danger that sections of it may start cracking, shifting and sinking into the soil. When this happens, you may ask yourself, “Why is this happening and what can be done to stop it?” There are a few common causes behind sinking concrete slabs. The most common are:
  1. Erosion
  2. Decomposition
  3. Settling / Disturbing native soil

What water problems can cause concrete damage?

Erosion is a common cause of voids forming below your concrete. Usually, it's caused by broken sprinkler lines and downspouts. The water in these leaks is already under the concrete and the water starts washing away the dirt, where it can't be seen. We get a lot of snow, hail, and rain here in Utah County and Salt Lake County; sometimes we get all three in one day! However, precipitation doesn’t have much of an impact on the concrete or the ground beneath it. However, the weather/temperature can cause a pipe to freezes, swells, and cracks in the winter. These cracks will begin to leak when it eventually thaws out again, and you might not realize it if it’s under a concrete slab, until the slab starts to disappear. Keep an eye on your water bill—if it spikes one month, you might want to call someone to have a look at your pipes before the erosion sets in.

What exactly is rotting under your concrete???

Not to worry...it isn’t likely that anything nefarious has taken place on your property, but there are things in the ground that can decompose and leave small voids. Things like:
  • Previous owners pets
  • Random things those pets buried in life
  • Time capsules
  • Tree roots (the most likely cause)
Tree roots can be a problem for concrete, while a tree is alive. The roots of trees eventually expand and raise/crack concrete slabs, even if the concrete is nowhere near the tree. Roots left behind from long-dead trees can result in small voids, but they are generally not large enough to cause a problem for your concrete. So again, not to worry, these minor cavities are not likely to have any impact on your concrete sidewalk or other slabs.

A house on a hill can’t be hidden… or supported.

Whether your home is on the side of a mountain, the top of a hill, or down in the valley, it’s unlikely that your entire property is completely level. Concrete is heavy and tends to settle over time. Whether it supports a house or just your kids’ bikes, there is a lot of weight in a small space and the ground underneath it isn’t as firm as slab itself. Shifting dirt is the most common and most serious cause of sinking concrete slabs. When the native soil is disturbed there can be areas of more and less densely packed dirt. So, your home might have been built on a previous lot with a back-filled basement, that dirt is now shifting and settling and can't hold up the concrete anymore. If your property wasn't properly compacted before concrete sidewalks or slabs were poured, the variation of density beneath your feet will start to even out and the sidewalk may start to sink.

What you can do to fix your sunken sidewalk or concrete slab

It really isn’t important, in the grand scheme of things, if your slab is sinking because of erosion, an ancient pet burial ground or an unsettling foundation. The fact is you have a problem and need it fixed. The traditional way would be to get a team out there with picks and hammers, let them make a big mess, then re-pour the section of sidewalk. Just wait one week and you’ll be back to normal, not to mention the high cost of labor, time and material you’ll have to pay for. An added benefit, your new concrete won’t match the rest of your sidewalk’s texture, color or shape...#ConversationPiece!

-Or-

You could give us a call. Landmark Lifting uses a polyurethane foam compound that lifts your slab back into its original position in a matter of minutes!
  • Our compound is inert, which means it won’t leach chemicals into the groundwater.
  • Our foam expands in 15 seconds
  • Our foam can hold 6,000 lbs per square foot.
  • Our foam cures in 15 - 30 minutes
Let us fix your sidewalk for you and you’ll be back on it by the time we’re done packing up our tools. Doesn’t that sound good? Call us at (801) 420-5117

title: The Hidden Enemy: How Water Penetration Damages Your Concrete
content:
When it comes to maintaining your property’s value and safety, concrete often gets taken for granted. It’s strong, durable, and seemingly indestructible. But there's a silent enemy that can slowly and steadily compromise your concrete's integrity and water penetration.

While it might not seem like a major threat, water is one of the most destructive forces when it comes to concrete structures. Left unchecked, moisture can lead to cracking, sinking, spalling, and even structural failure. At Landmark Lifting, we’ve seen firsthand the kind of damage water can do and we know how to stop it in its tracks.

Why Concrete is Vulnerable to Water

Concrete is a porous material. Even though it looks solid, it’s filled with tiny holes and capillaries that absorb and hold moisture. Over time, this water can wreak havoc, especially in areas that experience freeze-thaw cycles, heavy rainfall, or poor drainage.

When water seeps into concrete and temperatures drop, the water freezes and expands. This expansion puts pressure on the surrounding material, causing cracks and deterioration. When the ice melts, water can flow deeper into the concrete, only to freeze again during the next cold snap. This freeze-thaw cycle is one of the most common causes of concrete failure.

But even in warmer climates, water penetration leads to long-term issues, such as soil erosion beneath slabs, corrosion of embedded steel, and decreased load-bearing capacity.

Common Signs of Water Damage in Concrete

Water damage isn't always obvious at first. Here are a few warning signs to watch for:

  • Cracking or crumbling concrete: Surface cracks can indicate that water has entered the slab and is compromising its structure from within.
  • Pooling water or soggy soil: Water that doesn't drain properly around walkways, driveways, or foundations can quickly lead to slab shifting or settlement.
  • Discoloration or efflorescence: White, chalky residue on your concrete can be a sign of water moving through the material and bringing salts to the surface.
  • Sinking or uneven slabs: As water erodes the soil underneath your concrete, it creates voids that lead to uneven or sunken surfaces.

If you notice any of these issues, it's important to address them sooner rather than later. Delaying repairs can result in more extensive (and expensive) damage.

How Water Leads to Concrete Settlement

One of the most significant consequences of water penetration is concrete settlement. When water continuously flows or sits beneath a slab, it washes away the supporting soil or causes it to become soft and unstable. This loss of support leads to uneven or sunken concrete, which creates not just aesthetic problems but real safety hazards.

Sidewalks, driveways, patios, and garage floors are especially prone to this kind of damage. Over time, this sinking can create tripping hazards, drainage issues, and even affect the foundation of your home.

Prevention and Protection

The best defense against water damage is proper drainage and regular maintenance. Here are a few steps homeowners can take to minimize water intrusion:

  • Keep gutters and downspouts clear and functioning: Ensure they direct water away from your home and concrete surfaces.
  • Regrade landscaping if necessary: Make sure the slope directs water away from structures, not toward them.
  • Seal your concrete: A high-quality sealer can help reduce water absorption, especially on exposed surfaces like driveways and patios.
  • Repair cracks quickly: Small cracks are an open door for water. Sealing them early can prevent more significant issues down the road.

How Landmark Lifting Can Help

Even with preventative measures, water damage can still occur. That’s where we come in. At Landmark Lifting, we specialize in restoring damaged concrete caused by water penetration through advanced lifting and leveling techniques.

Using polyurethane foam injection, we can lift sunken concrete back into place, fill voids caused by water erosion, and stabilize the underlying soil all without the mess and cost of full replacement. Our process is minimally invasive, fast-curing, and highly effective for addressing the effects of water damage on concrete surfaces.

Additionally, our team can help assess drainage issues and recommend long-term solutions to keep water away from your slabs in the future.

Don’t Let Water Win

Water may be a natural element, but when it comes to your concrete, it’s anything but harmless. From small cracks to significant settling, moisture can turn a solid surface into a major problem before you even realize what’s happening.

If you’re noticing signs of water damage or want to protect your property before issues arise, contact Landmark Lifting. We’ll help you understand what’s going on beneath the surface and offer reliable, long-lasting solutions that restore your concrete and your peace of mind.

title: Top 3 Reasons to Choose Concrete Lifting Over Concrete Replacement
content:
When you have voids under your concrete due to soil settling, it’s important to have leveling or concrete lifting done to correct this. Otherwise, you can end up with cracks or other damage in your concrete as it settles into these voids. Concrete replacement with a new concrete pour used to be a common way to handle this problem. However, now concrete lifting provides distinctive benefits over concrete replacement. Here’s why:

1. Short Timeframe 

When you want to have settling problems corrected in a shorter time frame, concrete lifting offers a big advantage over concrete replacement. Having concrete replaced with a new pour can take between one and four days to do overall. This might be inconvenient for you and your family when you’re having a new pour done at your home. If you have a commercial building, you might need to close your business, or at least limit access to it, while concrete replacement is being done.

Concrete lifting cuts this time down considerably for residential and commercial buildings. In fact, it takes between one and four hours to complete a concrete lifting job. At Landmark Lifting, we drill small holes in sunken concrete slabs and then inject polyurethane foam into these holes. Full expansion only takes about 15 seconds to occur, and your concrete is ready to bear weight again right away.

2. Fast Curing 

Concrete lifting provides exceptionally fast curing, unlike concrete replacement. When you have a new concrete pour done due to voids or other settling problems, it can take weeks or even months for it to fully cure. Temperature and weather conditions can lead to even longer curing times. It also requires no driving on the new concrete for 2 weeks, so it’s a huge inconvenience for driveways and garages.

Concrete lifting takes less than 20 minutes to cure. Once it’s completely cured, your concrete will be able to hold thousands of pounds. Rather than having to wait weeks or months for this to happen, you only have to wait minutes for your concrete to be ready for use.

3. Cost-effective and Eco-friendly 

Concrete lifting can typically be done for about half the cost of concrete replacement since it requires less time and labor overall. This can lead to significant savings for you as a homeowner or commercial property owner.

When you choose Landmark Lifting, you’ll also have concrete lifting done that’s eco-friendly. We use a specially formulated polyurethane expanding foam to fill voids and level concrete. This eco-friendly foam contains 40 percent recycled materials and does not contain any chemicals that will seep into the groundwater or soil.

title: Uneven Patio in Sandy Utah
content:
What to do if you have an uneven patio concrete slab

Welcome to Sandy Utah. Today's home as an extensive concrete pad running from the driveway in the front yard, around the side of the garage and into the back yard. There is a lot of concrete on this property and that means that there is a lot of weight resting on the dirt and foundations underneath the concrete.

When houses are built, the ground is graded and leveled, which involves taking some dirt from one area and packing it in, in other areas. Mixing loose dirt with dirt that has settled naturally is a little like pouring sand in next to clay, it's not going to be as strong. That new dirt is usually the cause of underground voids, and those are where problems with concrete begin.

Voids under concrete are caused by:

  • Loose dirt settling and compacting over time
  • Snow and rain eroding loose dirt away
  • A broken pipe underground that washes the dirt away

The last is by far the most common, as broken pipes deliver a concentrated stream of pressurized water, and will continue until the problem is noticed.

Thankfully, at this home, the damage hadn't spread too far and we were able to drill a few dime-sized holes in the sunken concrete slab and inject our eco-friendly expansion foam under the concrete. As our foam expands, in a matter of seconds, the concrete is evenly and safely raised back to its original height. Within 15 minutes, the concrete was firm and stable, the underground void was filled and the patio was ready to bear weight again!

If you've got uneven concrete around your home or office, or inside a warehouse, it can be a potential trip hazard and if left alone the problem can spread. Call Landmark Lifting to schedule your consultation and get your concrete lifted quickly and permanently at a great price.

title: Uneven Sidewalks and Walkways: Causes, Solutions, and Prevention
content:
It often begins as a subtle shift. You might notice a slight lip on your front walkway while walking out to the mailbox in Alpine, Utah, or a minor misalignment along your path in Mapleton. Over the course of a few seasons, however, that minor variance can develop into a significant trip hazard and a liability concern. When property owners notice their concrete beginning to shift, tilt, or sink, the immediate question is almost always: What is causing this movement? While online resources frequently point to Utah’s extreme weather and intense winter freeze-thaw cycles as the primary culprits, local climate conditions are rarely the sole cause. At Landmark Lifting, we specialize in diagnosing and resolving concrete settling issues daily. Below, we break down the true underlying causes of uneven concrete, the common pitfalls of DIY repair methods, and how addressing these issues early can protect your property investment.

The Primary Causes of Uneven Concrete in Utah

When diagnosing structural shifting in residential concrete, several critical factors, or "top dogs", consistently emerge as the root causes:

Soil Instability: The #1 Factor

Soil conditions are the single greatest contributor to concrete movement. Utah soils naturally shift, expand, and contract. When the underlying soil base moves or loses its load-bearing capacity, the heavy concrete slab above settles along with it.

Improper Compaction During Construction

This issue is particularly common in newer developments across American Fork and Mapleton. If the subgrade was not thoroughly compacted using professional equipment before the concrete was poured, the ground will naturally settle over time, causing the walkway to drop.

Erosion and Subsurface Water Subversion

Underground water migration actively washes away the structural soil base supporting your slabs, creating hidden voids.

The Freeze-Thaw Cycle

While frequently blamed, environmental freeze-thaw cycles typically rank third to fifth on the list of primary causes. It is a major contributing factor, but it generally exacerbates pre-existing issues caused by poor soil stability or inadequate compaction.

Water: The Hidden Catalyst for Erosion

Water is the primary catalyst for accelerated concrete failure. When a control joint or structural crack is left unsealed, rainwater and snowmelt cannot properly sheet off the surface toward the street and storm drains. Instead, the water channels directly down into the joint. Once beneath the surface, it erodes the supporting soil, carving out voids that leave the slab completely unsupported. This issue is frequently compounded by broken irrigation lines or poorly positioned rain gutter downspouts that saturate the subgrade, forcing the concrete to crack and sink under its own weight. Is an uneven walkway creating a safety hazard on your property? Prevent subsurface voids from causing widespread damage. Contact the professional team at Landmark Lifting today for a comprehensive evaluation.

The Risks of DIY Concrete Repairs

Approximately 25% to 30% of homeowners attempt to patch or level sinking concrete themselves. While local property owners are often highly capable, DIY approaches to structural concrete often lead to unintended complications. The most common error in DIY remediation is using incorrect materials. Consumer hardware stores offer a wide variety of patching compounds and grouts, but selecting a product unsuited to the specific structural demands of the slab ensures the repair will quickly fail. Furthermore, attempting to mechanically hoist or jack a settled slab without specialized equipment introduces uneven pressure points. This frequently results in the irreversible cracking of the entire slab. Successful concrete leveling requires commercial-grade equipment and extensive field experience to accurately predict how a slab will respond to pressure.

Timelines and the Cost of Delayed Repair

For newly constructed homes in Utah County, the most significant soil settlement typically occurs within the first one to five years. By year ten, the soil generally returns to a stable, or “native” state. If you notice a driveway or walkway has settled an inch or more during this initial window, it has likely experienced the bulk of its projected movement. However, leaving the concrete unaddressed poses financial risks. The most effective strategy for managing concrete infrastructure is early intervention.
Early Remediation (Proactive) Delayed Intervention (Reactive)
• Multiple specialized repair options remain viable. • Total structural failure; removal is the only option.
• Adjustments are minor, localized, and highly efficient. • Requires comprehensive site reconstruction.
• Average cost ranges from a few hundred to $1,000+. • Replacement costs escalate from $6,000 to $20,000+.
• Arrests ongoing subgrade erosion immediately. • Leads to extensive subgrade destruction.
Addressing a settling walkway early ensures the repair remains minimally invasive and highly cost-effective. Polyurethane lifting and professional joint stabilization can restore a slab quickly. Waiting until the concrete is too far gone limits your options exclusively to full demolition and replacement, turning a manageable maintenance task into an expensive capital expenditure.

Comprehensive Solutions: When Replacement is Required

In cases where a concrete slab is excessively fractured or structurally compromised, lifting may no longer be a viable option. To streamline the restoration process for our clients, Landmark Lifting operates as a comprehensive, single-source contractor. We manage the entire lifecycle of your concrete, from poly-jacking and joint caulking to complete removal, pouring, and protective epoxy coatings. When a full replacement is required, we utilize sustainable practices by transporting your old concrete to our facility, where it is processed into high-quality recycled concrete road base. This material is then returned to the site to establish a perfectly graded, thoroughly compacted gravel foundation. Our team ensures the subgrade is precisely measured 4 inches below the finish line, installs necessary pipe sleeves for irrigation and drainage lines, and slopes the finished surface to guarantee water drains away from your home's foundation.

Establishing Realistic Expectations

A fundamental reality of concrete engineering is that, despite employing best practices, concrete is naturally prone to minor cracking over long cycles of time. Even with high-strength commercial mixes, proper rebar reinforcement, and optimal subgrade compaction, environmental shifting can still impact a slab over the span of decades. However, by establishing a solid foundation, maintaining proper joint sealants, and leveling uneven slabs early, you can successfully mitigate major structural failures and maximize the lifespan of your property's walkways.

Schedule a Professional Consultation with Landmark Lifting

Managing your property's concrete infrastructure does not have to be a guessing game. Partner with a trusted, reliable, local team known for clear communication, punctual service, and transparent assessments. Ready to eliminate trip hazards and restore the curb appeal of your property? Connect with the Landmark Lifting team today to arrange an on-site consultation and estimate across Mapleton, Alpine, American Fork, and the greater Utah County and Salt Lake Valley.
